issues.legal_issue: Interest payable on compensation for compulsorily acquired land includes interest on the statutory solatium component.
material_facts: The proceedings concerned compensation for land acquired compulsorily under the land acquisition law.
The compensation included solatium awarded because the acquisition was compulsory.
The dispute was whether interest payable on compensation also accrued on the solatium component.
issues.conclusion: A person entitled to compensation for acquired land is entitled to interest on the aggregate compensation, including solatium, when interest is payable under the applicable statutory provision.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 23(1), 23(1-A) and 23(2), the amounts awarded under each subsection together constitute the compensation awarded; Sections 28 and 34 provide for interest on that compensation, and do not permit it to be split into components to exclude solatium. Sections 26 and 31 support treating the additional amounts under Section 23 as part of the award and compensation payable. Solatium for compulsory acquisition is distinct from damages for a landowner’s disinclination to part with land, which Section 24 excludes from consideration. Union of India v. Shri Ram Mehar concerned interest on market value under a different amending provision and does not govern interest on compensation under Sections 28 and 34. Periyar & Pareekanni Rubbers Ltd. supports interest on solatium; the contrary views in Mir Fazeelath Hussain and Yadavrao P. Pathade are not followed, and the observation in Prem Nath Kapur was made where the question was not directly considered. The Court also noted consistent High Court decisions, including State of Haryana v. Smt. Kailashwati.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The proceeding concerns compensation for land acquired compulsorily.
predicates.solatium_awarded: The compensation awarded includes an additional amount because the acquisition was compulsory.
predicates.statutory_interest_payable: Interest is payable on the compensation because payment was delayed or an excess compensation amount was awarded.

issues.definition: When a land-acquisition proceeding includes solatium and statutory interest is payable, the interest extends to the solatium as part of the compensation.
